issues.description: Constructor parameter order for Meal is inconsistent: the problem statement (UML) and the solution expect Meal(String name, String[] ingredients), but the template defines the constructor as Meal(String[] ingredients, String name). This will confuse students and break example usage in Main where Meal is constructed as new Meal("cowBoyStew", new String[]{...}).
issues.suggestedFix: Change the Meal constructor in the template to match the specification and solution: public Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) { this.name = name; this.ingredients = ingredients; } This aligns the template with the UML, example usage in Main, and the reference solution.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML) and the solution expect Meal to be constructed as Meal(String name, String[] ingredients), but the template defines the constructor with the parameters reversed (Meal(String[] ingredients, String name)). This mismatch in constructor signature/order creates confusion for students when mapping the problem requirements to the provided template and the expected solution usage.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template Meal constructor signature to match the problem and solution: public Meal(String name, String[] ingredients). Also update any template Main/test code usage if necessary so construction uses (name, ingredients).
